# Simplify regression tests -- pipe-delimited
# Fields: name | input | reference | skip_string_compare | render_options
# render_options: blank = C's Channel defaults (comments on, indent 3).
#                 `comment=0,indent=0` reproduces a reference captured with
#                 those Channel attributes turned off. An unknown key is a hard
#                 error, so a typo cannot quietly widen the comparison.
# skip_string_compare: blank = compare the simplified dump byte-for-byte
#                             against the reference (numeric tokens to 4 ulp)
#                             as well as by astequal
#                      yes  = astequal only; every such entry carries a comment
#                             above it recording the diagnosed reason
#
# A negative fixture names the same file as both input and reference: the
# assertion is that `simplify` returns the Mapping unchanged. Those keep the
# byte-exact comparison; the harness ignores only the `IsSimp` line, which C's
# `astSimplify` stamps on every result it returns (mapping.c:24759) and which a
# never-simplified reference therefore cannot carry.

# spec_cel_invert.{map,simp} capture a FITS cube's pixel→world Mapping (FREQ
# spectral axis + celestial axes) just before/after C `astSimplify`
# (fitschan.c:37810). The input map8 ends with an inverted WcsMap; the spectral
# shift swaps past it via try_swap_winmap_wcsmap. Regression guard for the
# WinMap↔WcsMap swap dropping each map's invert flag (was double-swapping the
# flags so an inverted neighbour negated the linear map's shift, producing a
# spectral axis off by 2*CRVAL).
spec_cel_invert | simplify_fixtures/spec_cel_invert.map | simplify_fixtures/spec_cel_invert.simp |

# Scenario fixtures (integration regressions, stay in ast_tester/).
#
# lsst.simp was captured from a C run with the Channel's Comment and Indent
# attributes off -- no inline `\t#` comments, and no nesting indentation. That
# was diagnosed as "our serializer always emits comments" and handled by
# skipping the byte comparison. It is not a port limitation: the renderer has
# always had both options, so the fix is to render the way the reference was
# captured, which is what the render_options field says. lsst is byte-exact
# under those options and needs no skip at all.
#
# rigby.simp was captured the same way, and was also stale: the pinned C at
# f6762005 reproduces neither its formatting nor its IsSimp placement. It has
# been regenerated from that C with the Channel defaults, so it now needs no
# render_options.
#
# rigby keeps its skip for two reasons, neither of them formatting. It emits
# one IsSimp card fewer than C (8 against 9) -- pinned by the
# ISSIMP_DISAGREEMENTS assertion, so that part is visible without the skip --
# and one inverse-matrix element comes out as -5.9658198263111446e-17 where C
# has -5.8980598183211441e-17. Both are noise around zero, but they differ by
# about 1% relatively, far outside the 4-ulp token tolerance. rigby exercises
# the celestial WinMat Scl->1.0 path (see project_rigby_winmat_trace), which is
# where that residue comes from.
brad  | brad.map  | brad.simp  |
lsst1 | lsst1.map | lsst1.simp |
lsst  | lsst.ast  | lsst.simp  | | comment=0,indent=0
rigby | rigby.map | rigby.simp | yes |

# Negative (guard-rejection) fixtures: same file in both columns, astequal only.
#
# These prove a map that should NOT simplify is returned structurally
# unchanged. The reference is the raw un-simplified input (no `IsSimp` tag).
# Rust's `simplify()` always tags its returned map `IsSimp = 1` even when it
# made no change, so the ONLY serialization difference from the reference is
# that one tag line — the transform and every other token match byte-for-byte.
# The byte-exact string diff would flag that tag; astequal ignores it, so these
# run astequal-only. (Exceptions carry their own inline note below:
# neg_box_asymmetric_2d is byte-exact and runs the full diff;
# neg_time_5arg_mismatch additionally differs by a single last-ulp digit in one
# TimeMap argument — see its entry.)
neg_matrix_diag_unequal | simplify_fixtures/neg_matrix_diag_unequal.map | simplify_fixtures/neg_matrix_diag_unequal.map |

# unitnormmap_nonunit_scale was written as a negative fixture -- input named as
# its own reference, asserting simplify leaves it alone. It is not one. The
# WinMap's shift terms are all zero, and C `winmap.c::MapMerge` replaces such a
# WinMap with a diagonal MatrixMap as its first step, "without reference to the
# neighbouring Mappings in the list" (winmap.c:210-250). Probed against the
# reference library: C returns CmpMap{MatrixMap, UnitNormMap}, not the input.
# The port passed the old assertion by accident -- it reduced the leaf during
# decomposition, then the no-pairwise-change fast path discarded the reduced
# leaf and re-emitted the original tree. Given a real reference, generated the
# way ast_tester/gen_simplify_fixtures.c generates them, it is an ordinary
# positive case.

# C library astSimplify preserve the same ~1e-16 residue inherited from
# build_pixel_to_iwc — the residue is mathematically real, not a simplifier
# gap. Byte-exact with the C reference once the simplifier reconstructs the
# inverted-CmpMap decomposition (the MapList "simpler" flag) and records each
# component's effective direction in InvA/InvB while serialising it in its

# DssMap MapMerge fixtures (dssmap-03/07/08 from simplify_pathways.md). In the
# C library these are marked "infeasible: protected constructor" — the public
# C API cannot build a DssMap to drive its MapMerge. The .map inputs were
# generated by the Rust serializer (DssMap::from_plate_params is public) and
# the .simp references by the reference C library's astSimplify reading those
# native dumps (C reads a DssMap dump without converting it). dssmap-07: a
# non-inverted DssMap absorbs a preceding WinMap; dssmap-08: an inverted
# DssMap absorbs a following WinMap; dssmap-03: a ZoomMap neighbour is not
# absorbed (stays a CmpMap).

# Same-class run merges (gap-doc 6g): C's SpecMap/TimeMap/SlaMap MapMerge scans
# the whole list and accumulates an entire run of adjacent same-class maps into
# one combined step list before cancelling. Rust uses iterated pairwise CmpMap
# merging instead. These fixtures (runs of 3-4 maps, including an inverted
# middle map and partial cancellations) prove the two algorithms produce
# identical results — generated by the reference C library's astSimplify.

# ============================================================
# New fixtures imported from upstream 50c2b21b (simplify sweep).
# ============================================================

# cap_cmpmap_01, cap_cmpmap_04 and cap_specmap_02 are astequal-only (skip the
# byte-exact string diff). Their transforms and structure match C exactly; the
# ONLY divergence is where one `Invert` line sits: cap_cmpmap_01 and _04 place
# it on the enclosing CmpMap rather than on its child.
#
# That is the `InvA`/`InvB` quirk, still open upstream: C's `CombineMaps`
# records the child's Invert on the parent when the two CmpMaps share a
# pointer, so the pair the dump carries reflects C's reference counting rather
# than the Mapping. See docs/issues/c-library-quirks.md, "CmpMap dumps
# InvA/InvB disagreeing with the child's own Invert". The port holds components
# by value and has no such history to record. Compared by astequal only until
# that quirk is settled upstream.
#
# Measured 2026-08-20, after leaf reduction moved out of the decomposition:
# apart from that one Invert line, cap_cmpmap_01 differs by two IsSimp cards
# (16 against C's 18) and cap_cmpmap_04 by three (15 against 18). So both would
# still need the counted IsSimp licence even once the Invert quirk is settled;
# the blanket skip is not covering only the tag. Everything else in both files
# matches, including the Invert cards on every other node.

# --- Supported classes ---

# --- Unsupported classes: fixtures exercising Mapping/Region classes not
# --- yet ported (IntraMap, XphMap, StcResourceProfile) have been moved to
# --- ../simplify_fixtures_unsupported/<class>/ so they are excluded from
# --- both the simplify regression and the byte-exact round-trip corpus.
# --- Move them back into simplify_fixtures/ and add manifest entries here
# --- when those classes land. See simplify_fixtures_unsupported/README.md.

# A lone MJDTOJD or JDTOMJD step whose offsets absorb the 2400000.5 constant is
# a change of system with no effect, and C's MapMerge drops it
# (timemap.c:2260-2266), leaving a UnitMap. time_2arg_swapped_cancel also
# reaches a UnitMap, but by cancelling an inverse pair, so it does not exercise
# this rule. The negative control keeps a conversion whose offsets do not
# absorb the constant.
time_mjdtojd_noop | simplify_fixtures/time_mjdtojd_noop.map | simplify_fixtures/time_mjdtojd_noop.simp |
time_jdtomjd_noop | simplify_fixtures/time_jdtomjd_noop.map | simplify_fixtures/time_jdtomjd_noop.simp |
neg_time_mjdtojd_real | simplify_fixtures/neg_time_mjdtojd_real.map | simplify_fixtures/neg_time_mjdtojd_real.map |

# An inverted UnitMap in parallel with a Mapping that cannot absorb it: C
# clears the list's invert flag for it and reports a change
# (unitmap.c:579-587), which surfaces as the parent CmpMap dropping its InvA.
# The neighbour is a PcdMap because it combines with nothing in parallel
# (pcdmap.c:1729); unit_parallel_invert_clear covers the same rule with a
# MathMap neighbour and one fewer axis.
unit_parallel_invert_pcd | simplify_fixtures/unit_parallel_invert_pcd.map | simplify_fixtures/unit_parallel_invert_pcd.simp |
neg_unit_parallel_forward | simplify_fixtures/neg_unit_parallel_forward.map | simplify_fixtures/neg_unit_parallel_forward.map |

# A zero-distortion PcdMap is a UnitMap, and C's MapMerge replaces it before
# considering any neighbour (pcdmap.c:1417-1433). pcd_zero_disc_series puts it
# between two MatrixMaps that can only merge with each other once it has gone,
# so the replacement has to reach a nominee inside the list; pcd_zero_disc_lone
# reaches the same replacement through the base Simplify.
pcd_zero_disc_series | simplify_fixtures/pcd_zero_disc_series.map | simplify_fixtures/pcd_zero_disc_series.simp |
pcd_zero_disc_lone | simplify_fixtures/pcd_zero_disc_lone.map | simplify_fixtures/pcd_zero_disc_lone.simp |
